correctness.rationale: A uniform sequence of element-toggle matchings is acyclic for every n>=3. The endpoint toggle on Ind_2(P_m) leaves exactly the compulsory edge plus Ind_2(P_{m-4}), with explicit m=0,1,2,3 bases. Toggling a triangle vertex partitions the residual faces into one shifted Ind_2(P_{n-3}) and two shifted Ind_2(P_{n-4}) families (n>=4), plus an explicit n=3 case. All resulting critical faces have one positive dimension for fixed n, with counts 3,2,0,1 in residues 3,0,1,2. Thus the CW model has one basepoint and the stated sphere wedge or point. The standard-library verifier independently checks all faces, acyclic Hasse orientations, global versus fiber pivot equivalence and Euler characteristics for n=3..16 and ordinary mod-two simplicial boundary ranks for n=3..10; finite checks supplement, not replace, the induction.

value.rationale: A natural first bicyclic cactus family, a vertex-glued triangle and arbitrary cycle, is completely classified for a nontrivial higher-independence functor. It provides a genuine all-length four-residue transition between three spheres, two spheres, contractibility, and one sphere; the hub coupling prevents using the join of known cycle results. The uniform three-fiber discrete-Morse resolution supplies a reusable structural idea beyond isolated numerical cases. No assertion about general cactus graphs or arbitrary r is needed.
